_meta.notes: Per-sport facts generated by scripts/generate-sport-facts.ts using Claude with web search, grounded on Paris 2024 medal results.

Ceremony.gamesContext: Ceremonies are non-competitive, so no medals are awarded. They open and close the 2028 Summer Games. The Opening Ceremony is scheduled for July 14, 2028, and organizers say it will be the first opening ceremony ever split across two stadiums at once. Competition is set to run through July 30, 2028, when the Closing Ceremony will hand the Games over to the next host. Both ceremonies usually include a parade of athletes and an artistic program. The opening also features the traditional cauldron lighting, while the closing includes the flag handover to the next host city.
Ceremony.parisRecap: No medals were awarded because ceremonies are not a competition. The Paris 2024 Opening Ceremony on July 26, 2024 was the first to hold the athletes' parade outside a stadium. About 85 boats carried roughly 6,800 athletes along the Seine toward the Eiffel Tower in a rain-soaked show directed by French theater director Thomas Jolly. The Closing Ceremony on August 11, 2024 included a performance by the French band Phoenix and the official handover to Los Angeles. In that segment, Tom Cruise rappelled from the stadium roof to carry the flag, and a pre-recorded section in Los Angeles featured Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers, with H.E.R. performing the U.S. anthem.

Athletics (Track & Field).gamesContext: Athletics returns as a core sport of the 2028 Summer Games with 48 medal events: 23 for men, 23 for women and 2 mixed. In a break from tradition, track and field moves to the first week and swimming to the second. Track and field runs over a record 13 days, July 15 to 30, with ten days of stadium action from July 15 to 24 and the road events on July 27, 29 and 30. The men's marathon is the final event, and its medals are awarded at the closing ceremony. Day 1 packs all four rounds of the women's 100m, starting with the preliminary round for lower-ranked sprinters and ending with the semifinal and final that evening, plus the women's shot put and men's 10,000m finals. The program changes from Paris 2024: a mixed 4x100m relay makes its debut, half marathon race walks (about 21.1 km) replace the 20 km walks, and the marathon race walk mixed relay is dropped after a single appearance. Sprint, hurdle and middle-distance events again use the heats, repechage, semifinal and final format.
Athletics (Track & Field).parisRecap: Paris 2024 produced three world records. Mondo Duplantis cleared 6.25m to win the pole vault, Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone ran 50.37 to win the women's 400m hurdles ahead of Anna Cockrell and Femke Bol, and the United States set a mixed 4x400m record in the heats, though the Netherlands took gold in the final. Noah Lyles won a photo-finish men's 100m ahead of Kishane Thompson and later took bronze in the 200m behind Letsile Tebogo, whose gold was Botswana's first in the event. Julien Alfred won Saint Lucia's first gold in the women's 100m, Gabby Thomas took the 200m, and Cole Hocker beat Josh Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen in the 1500m. Ingebrigtsen went on to win the 5000m. In distance running, Beatrice Chebet won both the 5000m and 10,000m, while Sifan Hassan added marathon gold to bronzes in both track events. Other highlights included Arshad Nadeem's javelin win over Neeraj Chopra, Rai Benjamin beating Karsten Warholm in the men's 400m hurdles, and Canada's upset gold in the men's 4x100m relay.

Athletics (Marathon).gamesContext: The marathon returns as a standard part of the athletics program at the 2028 Games, with two medal events: the men's and women's marathon. Each is a single-race final with no heats. Following tradition, the marathons are scheduled for the final weekend of the Games: the women's race on July 29, 2028, and the men's race on July 30 as the last athletics event of the Games. This reverses Paris 2024, where the women's marathon was the final athletics event. Both races are set to start at the Venice Beach Boardwalk. Organizers have said full road-race routes, including the marathon finish, will be published at a later date.
Athletics (Marathon).parisRecap: In Paris 2024, both marathons were run on a hilly course and both winners set new Games records. Ethiopia's Tamirat Tola had been a late addition to the Ethiopian team. He broke away on the course's steepest climb around 28 km and won in 2:06:26, finishing ahead of Belgium's Bashir Abdi (silver) and Kenya's Benson Kipruto (bronze). In the women's race, the Netherlands' Sifan Hassan won in 2:22:55 after a sprint duel with Ethiopia's Tigst Assefa, who took silver, while Kenya's Hellen Obiri won bronze. Hassan's win came just days after she won bronze in both the 5,000m and the 10,000m, so she left Paris with medals in three distance events.

Athletics (Race Walk).gamesContext: Race walking returns at the 2028 Summer Games over a new distance. The men's and women's 20 km walks are replaced by men's and women's half-marathon (21.1 km) race walks, in line with World Athletics' move to half-marathon and marathon walk distances. There are two medal events, both straight finals with no heats, and both are scheduled for a single morning session on Thursday, July 27, 2028, when the road events take over after the track program ends. The mixed marathon race walk relay that debuted in Paris has been dropped to make room for the new mixed 4x100m relay, which drew public criticism from walkers such as Canada's Evan Dunfee, who called it part of the "ongoing TikTokification" of the Games.
Athletics (Race Walk).parisRecap: At Paris 2024 the race walks started and finished at Pont d'Iéna. Ecuador's Brian Pintado won the men's 20 km ahead of Brazil's Caio Bonfim, with Spain's Álvaro Martín taking bronze. China's Yang Jiayu won the women's 20 km, beating Spain's María Pérez to silver, with Australia's Jemima Montag in bronze. Paris was the only time the mixed marathon race walk relay was held: Spain took gold, Ecuador silver and Australia bronze, so Spain, Ecuador and Australia each won medals in two of the three walking events.

Swimming.gamesContext: Swimming returns at the 2028 Games with an expanded program of 41 pool medal events: 20 for men, 20 for women, and the mixed 4x100m medley relay. Six events are new since Paris 2024: the men's and women's 50m backstroke, 50m breaststroke and 50m butterfly. Those sprint races were approved in April 2025 and use a heats, semifinals and final format, like the other short-distance events. In a major schedule change, swimming moves to the second week of the Games and trades places with athletics, which usually runs in week two. The pool program runs over nine days, with morning heats and evening semifinals and finals, while the 800m and 1500m freestyle, 400m IM and relays go straight from heats to finals.
Swimming.parisRecap: France's Léon Marchand was the star of Paris 2024, winning four individual golds in the 200m breaststroke, 200m butterfly, 200m IM and 400m IM, and he won the butterfly and breaststroke finals on the same night. Canada's Summer McIntosh won three golds (200m butterfly, 200m IM and 400m IM) plus silver in the 400m freestyle behind Ariarne Titmus. Katie Ledecky won the 800m and 1500m freestyle, and Sarah Sjöström won the sprint freestyle double. Pan Zhanle won the men's 100m freestyle in a world record, and China then beat the United States in the men's medley relay. Australia's women won both freestyle relays, and Kaylee McKeown won both backstroke events. Adam Peaty finished in a tie for silver in the men's 100m breaststroke behind Nicolò Martinenghi, so no bronze was awarded in that race.

Artistic Gymnastics.gamesContext: Artistic gymnastics is back on the 2028 Summer Games program. It keeps its standard structure: subdivided qualification rounds for men and women, then team finals, individual all-around finals and apparatus finals. The big change from Paris 2024 is a new Mixed Team event, announced in April 2025 as one of several mixed-gender additions. That raises the medal count from 14 to 15. The world governing body, FIG, is still working out the mixed team's format and eligibility, and the session schedule lists its format and duration as pending FIG approval. A mixed team final was trialed at the 2025 European Championships, where the top 16 qualifying pairs advanced to the final.
Artistic Gymnastics.parisRecap: Simone Biles led the United States to the women's team title ahead of Italy and Brazil. She also won the all-around and vault, finishing ahead of Rebeca Andrade both times, but Andrade beat her for floor gold. Italy had a breakthrough Games: team silver, then a one-three finish on beam for Alice D'Amato and Manila Esposito. Kaylia Nemour won Algeria's first gymnastics gold on uneven bars, and Ana Barbosu of Romania was awarded floor bronze. On the men's side, Japan beat China for team gold, and Shinnosuke Oka won three golds (team, all-around and horizontal bar) plus a bronze on parallel bars. Carlos Yulo won both floor and vault for the Philippines. Other men's apparatus titles went to Zou Jingyuan (parallel bars), Liu Yang (rings) and Ireland's Rhys McClenaghan (pommel horse), with pommel specialist Stephen Nedoroscik helping the United States to team bronze.

Basketball.gamesContext: Basketball comes back at the 2028 Games with two medal events, a men's and a women's tournament of 12 nations each. Teams play a group phase, then quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal games. The USA qualifies automatically as host in both. On the men's side, seven places come from the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 in Qatar and the rest from qualifying tournaments in mid-2028. The women's qualifying path starts with the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 in Germany, whose winner qualifies directly. The big storyline is whether the USA can extend its streaks of five straight men's titles and eight straight women's titles on home soil. 3x3 basketball is a separate medal discipline with its own qualifying system.
Basketball.parisRecap: The United States won both tournaments at Paris 2024, and host nation France took silver in both. The US men beat France 98-87 in the final on 10 August for their fifth straight title and 17th overall. Stephen Curry hit a run of late three-pointers to seal it, and Serbia took the men's bronze. The US women beat France 67-66 on 11 August for an eighth straight gold, the first team in any sport to win eight in a row. France's last shot to tie was a Gabby Williams attempt from just inside the arc, so it counted for two instead of three. Australia won the women's bronze.

Football (Soccer).gamesContext: Football returns at the 2028 Summer Games with two medal events, a men's tournament and a women's tournament, each played as a group stage followed by quarterfinals, semifinals, a bronze medal match and a gold medal match. The biggest change from Paris 2024 is the size of the fields: the women's tournament grows from 12 to 16 national teams, the first time it has had more than 12 since 2008, and the men's tournament shrinks from 16 to 12 teams. The change is part of a wider program decision that gives every team sport at least as many women's teams as men's teams. The men's event is expected to keep its mostly under-23 squad format. With the United States as host and defending women's champion, the home side's title defense is a central storyline, though which teams take part has not been confirmed.
Football (Soccer).parisRecap: Spain won the men's gold by beating host nation France 5-3 after extra time in the final at the Parc des Princes on August 9, 2024. Fermin Lopez scored twice in normal time and Sergio Camello scored in extra time, giving Spain its second-ever men's football gold. Morocco took bronze, the country's first medal in the sport. In the women's final on August 10, the United States beat Brazil 1-0 on a Mallory Swanson goal early in the second half, winning a record fifth women's gold after settling for bronze in Tokyo. Brazil took silver in what was expected to be Marta's last appearance at the Games, and Germany won the bronze.

Tennis.gamesContext: Tennis returns at the 2028 Games with five medal events: men's and women's singles, men's and women's doubles, and mixed doubles. Matches will be played on hard courts from July 19 to 28, 2028. The surface changes from the clay used at Paris 2024, and the event grows from nine days to ten. Because it starts only days after Wimbledon ends, tennis falls in the second week of the Games instead of the usual first week. Planned draws are 64 players in each singles event, 32 teams in each doubles event and 16 mixed doubles teams. In a new format, mixed doubles opens the event and is decided in two days: two rounds on day one, then the semifinals and medal matches on day two, when singles also begins. Medal matches for the other four events are set for July 27 and 28. Media coverage has named stars such as Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner and Coco Gauff as expected contenders, but no participation is confirmed.
Tennis.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, played on the clay at Roland Garros, Novak Djokovic of Serbia won his first singles gold by beating Carlos Alcaraz of Spain in a two-tiebreak final, completing a career Golden Slam. Lorenzo Musetti of Italy took bronze. Zheng Qinwen of China won the women's singles, beating Donna Vekic of Croatia in the final, while Iga Swiatek of Poland took bronze. Matthew Ebden and John Peers won men's doubles gold, Australia's first tennis gold in 28 years, saving their final in a 10-8 match tiebreak against Americans Rajeev Ram and Austin Krajicek, and Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul won bronze for the United States. Italy's Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini won the women's doubles in a final-set tiebreak against neutral athletes Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider, Spain took bronze, and Czechia's Katerina Siniakova and Tomas Machac won mixed doubles gold ahead of China's Wang Xinyu and Zhang Zhizhen, with Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Felix Auger-Aliassime taking bronze.

Diving.gamesContext: Diving returns at the 2028 Games with the same eight medal events as Paris 2024: individual 3m springboard and 10m platform for men and women, plus men's and women's synchronized 3m springboard and synchronized 10m platform. Individual events run as preliminary, semifinal and final rounds, while the synchronized events are decided in a single final. The world governing body for aquatics and the IOC have finalized the diving qualification system for the 2028 Games, which run 14 to 30 July 2028. The main storyline is whether anyone can break China's hold on the sport after its clean sweep in Paris, with Great Britain, Mexico, the United States, Australia, Japan and North Korea among the nations that won medals in Paris and could be in the hunt again.
Diving.parisRecap: China won all eight diving gold medals at Paris 2024, the first time any nation has swept every diving event. Cao Yuan finished off the sweep by defending his men's 10m platform title, ahead of Rikuto Tamai of Japan and Noah Williams of Great Britain, while reigning world champion Yang Hao placed only 12th. Quan Hongchan beat teammate Chen Yuxi for women's platform gold, Chen Yiwen won women's springboard ahead of Australia's Maddison Keeney, and Xie Siyi led a Chinese one-two over Wang Zongyuan in men's springboard, with Osmar Olvera of Mexico taking bronze. Great Britain won the most medals of any nation other than China, taking five medals (all silver or bronze) across the synchronized events and men's platform. Mexico, the United States and North Korea each won a silver in the synchronized events.

Volleyball.gamesContext: Indoor volleyball returns at the 2028 Summer Games as a fixture of the program, with two medal events: a men's and a women's tournament of 12 teams each (144 athletes per gender). Each tournament opens with a preliminary round, then the top teams move into single-elimination quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal matches. Under the qualification system approved in December 2025, one spot per gender goes to the host nation and the other 11 are filled through FIVB qualification pathways, including the FIVB World Ranking, with the qualification window running through June 2028. Storylines to watch include whether France can extend its run of men's titles, whether Italy's women can defend their first-ever gold, and whether the home United States teams, medalists in both events at Paris 2024, can turn that into gold.
Volleyball.parisRecap: France's men defended their title on home soil, sweeping world No. 1 Poland 3-0 (25-19, 25-20, 25-23) in the final. That made France the first men's team since the United States (1984 and 1988) to win back-to-back golds, with Jean Patry and Trevor Clevenot leading the way. Poland took silver in its first final in 48 years, and the United States won the men's bronze. On the women's side, Italy won its first-ever gold by sweeping the defending champion United States 3-0, Paola Egonu scored 22 points in the final and was named tournament MVP, and Brazil took the bronze.

Beach Volleyball.gamesContext: Beach volleyball returns at the 2028 Summer Games, a fixture of the program since 1996, with two medal events: men's and women's two-person team tournaments. Under the qualification system announced by the FIVB in December 2025, 48 teams qualify (24 men's and 24 women's). Each tournament runs from pool-play preliminaries to a single-elimination bracket: Round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, then bronze and gold medal matches. Paris 2024 champions Sweden (men) and Brazil (women) would be projected title contenders, but no 2028 rosters are confirmed. The home crowd in Southern California, where the sport is deeply rooted, adds interest for the U.S. teams.
Beach Volleyball.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, Sweden's 22-year-old David Ahman and Jonatan Hellvig were the top seeds in their first Games appearance. They beat Germany's Nils Ehlers and Clemens Wickler 21-10, 21-13 in the final for Sweden's first-ever gold in the sport, and Norway took men's bronze. In the women's final, Brazil's Ana Patricia and Duda beat Canada's Brandie Wilkerson and Melissa Humana-Paredes 26-24, 12-21, 15-10. It was the first women's final in the sport's history at the Games to go to three sets, and Brazil's first women's title since 1996. Switzerland won women's bronze. The tournament was played in a temporary stadium in front of the Eiffel Tower.

Baseball.gamesContext: Baseball returns to the 2028 Summer Games after being left off the Paris 2024 program. It was last played at Tokyo 2020, and before that it was a medal sport from 1992 to 2008. There is one medal event, a six-team men's tournament scheduled for July 13-19, 2028. It runs from an opening round to quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal games. The United States qualified automatically as host. The Dominican Republic and Venezuela earned their places at the 2026 World Baseball Classic, which was the first qualifying event for the 2028 Games in any sport. Venezuela, which went on to win that Classic, will be making its first appearance in this tournament. The last three places will come from the 2027 WBSC Premier12 (one Asian team and one from Europe or Oceania) and a final qualifier held no later than March 2028. MLB owners have reportedly backed pausing the season so active major leaguers can play, which would be a first. However, talks with the players' union over issues such as hotels, insurance and NIL rights had not been settled as of the latest reports, so MLB player participation is not confirmed.
Baseball.parisRecap: Baseball was not on the Paris 2024 program, so no medals were awarded in the sport there. The most recent tournament at the Summer Games was Tokyo 2020: host Japan won gold, the United States took silver, and the Dominican Republic won bronze by beating South Korea 10-6 in the bronze medal game.

Softball.gamesContext: Softball returns at the 2028 Games after being left off the Paris 2024 program. It will be the sport's sixth appearance, following 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008 and Tokyo 2020. Six women's teams play a single round-robin preliminary round from July 23 to 27, with three games per day. The top two teams then meet in the gold medal game and the third- and fourth-placed teams play for bronze, with both medal games scheduled by July 29. As host, the USA qualifies automatically. The other five places go to the best non-host finisher at the 2027 WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Finals, the winners of the Europe/Africa, Asia/Oceania and Americas qualifiers, and the winner of a Final Qualification Event that ends by March 2028. Japan (ranked No. 1 in the world) and the USA (No. 2) are the projected main contenders, which could set up a rematch of the Tokyo 2020 final.
Softball.parisRecap: Softball was not contested at Paris 2024, so there are no Paris medalists in this sport. The most recent tournament at the Games was Tokyo 2020, where Japan won gold, the United States took silver and Canada won bronze.

Flag Football.gamesContext: Flag football makes its debut at the 2028 Summer Games, one of five sports added for Los Angeles and the first time any form of gridiron football has been a full medal sport. There are two medal events, a men's and a women's tournament, each with six teams of 10 athletes (12 teams and 120 athletes in total), played five-a-side and run as preliminaries, semifinals, and then bronze and gold medal games. Places go to national committees through three routes, including host-nation allocation for the United States and the 2026 IFAF World Flag Football Championships in Dusseldorf, where Italy won the first men's spot and Canada earned a men's spot by taking bronze. The big storyline is that NFL clubs voted in May 2025 to let players under NFL contracts try out for national teams, with no more than one player per NFL club on a country's roster. Rosters are not yet confirmed.
Flag Football.parisRecap: Flag football was not on the Paris 2024 program, so there are no previous medalists or results at the Games. Its first appearance will be in 2028. Until then, the IFAF World Flag Football Championships, including the 2026 edition that doubled as a qualifier, are the sport's top international competition.

Cricket.gamesContext: Cricket is one of five sports added for the 2028 Games. It was approved in 2023 alongside baseball/softball, flag football, lacrosse (sixes) and squash. The sport's only previous appearance was at the 1900 Games in Paris, where Great Britain beat France in a single match. In 2028 it will be played in the Twenty20 (T20) format, with two medal events: a men's and a women's tournament of six teams each, and each team names a 15-player squad. Play moves from group-stage rounds to bronze and gold medal matches, with the tournament reported for roughly July 12–29, 2028. Under the ICC's qualification pathway, Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania are each guaranteed a team. Australia, Great Britain, India and South Africa earned the first women's places through the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup. The host United States can qualify directly in each event if it ranks in the top 15 of the T20I rankings, and the remaining places will be decided at eight-team ICC qualifiers scheduled for January–February 2028.
Cricket.parisRecap: Cricket was not on the Paris 2024 program, so there are no Paris medalists. The 2028 tournaments will be the sport's first appearance at a Summer Games since 1900. The most recent major T20 form reference before those Games came from the ICC world championships: India held the men's T20 world title and New Zealand the women's title when the 2028 event program was approved.

Lacrosse.gamesContext: Lacrosse returns to the Summer Games program in 2028 for the first time as a medal sport since 1908. It will be played in the fast-paced Sixes format, which World Lacrosse created in 2021, with six players per side, a smaller field and shorter games. There are two medal events, a six-team men's tournament and a six-team women's tournament, each running a round-robin qualifying stage followed by bronze and gold medal games. The United States qualifies automatically as host. The other places go through a three-stage pathway: 2026 continental championships, then the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships with 16 teams per gender, then a final qualifying tournament in early 2028.
Lacrosse.parisRecap: Lacrosse was not part of the Paris 2024 program, so there are no Paris 2024 medalists. The sport's last medal events were in 1904 and 1908. It also appeared as a demonstration sport in 1928, 1932 and 1948. The 2028 tournaments will be the first time women's lacrosse is played for medals at the Summer Games, and the first time the Sixes format is used.

Squash.gamesContext: Squash makes its debut on the 2028 Games program, approved by the IOC Session in Mumbai in October 2023 alongside baseball/softball, cricket, flag football and lacrosse. There are two medal events, men's singles and women's singles, each a 16-player single-elimination knockout bracket (Round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, then bronze and gold medal matches) scheduled for July 15-24, 2028, for 32 players in total. Players qualify through five routes: Continental Games (five places per gender, including the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya), a host country quota, PSA world rankings, one universality place per gender, and one final spot per gender decided at a 24-player qualifying tournament in Washington state on June 6-10, 2028. Because no previous Games has included squash, every medal awarded will be a first for the sport.
Squash.parisRecap: Squash was not held at Paris 2024 and has never been part of an earlier Summer Games program, so there are no previous medalists or Games results. The 2028 tournament will be the sport's first appearance.

3x3 Basketball.gamesContext: 3x3 basketball returns in 2028 for its third Games appearance, after debuting at Tokyo 2020 and featuring again at Paris 2024. It has two medal events, men's and women's. Each field grows from 8 to 12 teams, a change the IOC Executive Board approved in April 2025. The host USA qualifies automatically. Five more spots per gender go out through the FIBA 3x3 Federation Ranking as of December 1, 2027, and the last six come from four qualifying tournaments in 2028. Session listings show a new play-in round alongside pool play, then quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal games, held over roughly July 16-22, 2028.
3x3 Basketball.parisRecap: At Paris 2024 the Netherlands won men's gold, beating host France 18-17 in overtime when Worthy de Jong hit a two-pointer; de Jong was named tournament MVP. Lithuania took men's bronze, while Latvia, the Tokyo 2020 champion, won all seven of its pool games but was beaten by France in the semifinals and left without a medal. In the women's final Germany beat Spain 17-16 for its first title, led by MVP Sonja Greinacher, in a rematch of the 2021 Europe Cup final. The United States won women's bronze. Every game was played at a temporary venue on the Place de la Concorde.

Boxing - Finals.gamesContext: Boxing returns at the 2028 Games after its place on the programme was confirmed by unanimous vote in March 2025, and it will be the first Games tournament run by World Boxing, the new international federation that replaced the IBA-era arrangement used for the last two editions. The programme grows from 13 events in Paris to 14, with seven weight classes each for men (55, 60, 65, 70, 80, 90 and +90kg) and women (51, 54, 57, 60, 65, 70 and 75kg), the first time the sport has full gender parity, with 248 quota places split evenly. Most weight limits shift from the Paris categories, so the divisions do not line up one-to-one with 2024. The single-elimination bracket runs through semifinals to finals, and both semifinal losers receive bronze medals. Qualification runs through seven events starting in April 2027, and World Boxing now requires sex testing for women's division eligibility.
Boxing - Finals.parisRecap: Uzbekistan led the men's tournament with five of the seven golds: Hasanboy Dusmatov (flyweight), Abdumalik Khalokov (featherweight), Asadkhuja Muydinkhujaev (welterweight), Lazizbek Mullojonov (heavyweight), and Bakhodir Jalolov, who won super-heavyweight again over Spain's Ayoub Ghadfa. Cuba's Erislandy Álvarez beat France's Sofiane Oumiha for lightweight gold, and Ukraine's Oleksandr Khyzhniak took light-heavyweight, while Mexico's Marco Verde won welterweight silver. On the women's side China won three golds (Wu Yu, Chang Yuan, Li Qian) and Ireland's Kellie Harrington defended her lightweight title. The Paris tournament was overshadowed by the eligibility controversy around Imane Khelif (ALG) and Lin Yu-Ting (TPE), who both won gold, Khelif at welterweight and Lin at featherweight.

Boxing - Prelims.gamesContext: Boxing is back for the 2028 Games. It was left off the original program because of governance problems with its former federation, the IBA. In March 2025 the IOC Session voted unanimously to reinstate it, after World Boxing received provisional recognition as the sport's new international federation. For the first time there will be 14 medal events split evenly by gender, seven for men (55, 60, 65, 70, 80, 90 and +90kg) and seven for women (51, 54, 57, 60, 65, 70 and 75kg). Paris 2024 had 13 events, so this adds one women's weight class and reshapes the weight categories. Each division is a single-elimination tournament: preliminary rounds (R32 and R16), then quarterfinals, semifinals and finals, with two bronze medals per weight class. Qualification runs from April 2027 to May 2028, with the 2027 World Boxing Championships serving as a key qualifying event, and each nation can enter at most one boxer per weight class.
Boxing - Prelims.parisRecap: Uzbekistan dominated the men's side at Paris 2024, winning five of seven men's golds: Hasanboy Dusmatov (flyweight), Abdumalik Khalokov (featherweight), Asadkhuja Muydinkhujaev (welterweight), Lazizbek Mullojonov (heavyweight) and Bakhodir Jalolov, who beat Spain's Ayoub Ghadfa to defend his super-heavyweight title. The other two men's golds went to Cuba's Erislandy Álvarez at lightweight, who beat home favorite Sofiane Oumiha, and Ukraine's Oleksandr Khyzhniak at light-heavyweight. China led the women's events with three golds, from Wu Yu (flyweight), Chang Yuan (bantamweight) and Li Qian (middleweight), plus two silvers. Ireland's Kellie Harrington defended her lightweight title. The tournament was overshadowed by a gender-eligibility controversy around two boxers who won gold anyway: Algeria's Imane Khelif at welterweight and Chinese Taipei's Lin Yu-Ting at featherweight.

Surfing.gamesContext: Surfing returns for its third straight Summer Games in 2028 after debuting at Tokyo 2020. Paris 2024 had two medal events, men's and women's shortboard, and 2028 does too. Each gender has 24 surfers, 48 in total. The competition runs as heat-based rounds, then quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal matches, with the timing depending on wave conditions. The qualification system changed after Paris. Results from the ISA World Surfing Games carry more weight, nations can qualify up to three athletes per gender (up from two), and after athlete pushback the ISA set the World Surf League Championship Tour allocation at eight men and eight women. The ISA also asked for more shortboard places and for longboard to be added, but neither was part of the confirmed 2028 program.
Surfing.parisRecap: The Paris 2024 surfing contest was held at the heavy reef break of Teahupo'o in Tahiti, and the final day only went ahead after two days of delays for poor conditions. Local French Polynesian Kauli Vaast won men's gold for France. He opened the final with a 9.50 and beat Australia's Jack Robinson 17.67 to 7.83, while Brazil's Gabriel Medina took bronze. The women's final went down to the last minutes. Caroline Marks of the USA beat Brazil's Tatiana Weston-Webb 10.50 to 10.33, a margin of 0.17, becoming the second American to win the event after Carissa Moore in 2021. Johanne Defay of France won bronze.

Skateboarding.gamesContext: Skateboarding comes back for its third straight Summer Games in 2028. It is one of the sport's homecomings, since modern skateboarding grew up in Southern California, and it moves from an optional host-city addition in 2020 and 2024 to the core sports program. There are four medal events, the same lineup as Paris 2024: men's and women's street and men's and women's park. Each event has 22 athletes, with preliminary rounds leading to finals. Places are decided mainly by the World Skateboarding Ranking, built from World Skate events, and qualifying started with the World Skateboarding Tour stop in Rome.
Skateboarding.parisRecap: Japan's Yuto Horigome kept his men's street title, landing the highest-scoring trick of the final in the last round to win gold. Americans Jagger Eaton (silver) and Nyjah Huston (bronze) completed the podium. The women's street podium was all teenagers: 14-year-old Coco Yoshizawa won gold ahead of Japanese teammate Liz Akama, and Brazil's Rayssa Leal took bronze. Australia won both park events, with Keegan Palmer keeping his men's title ahead of American Tom Schaar and Brazil's Augusto Akio, and Arisa Trew winning the women's event ahead of Japan's Kokona Hiraki and Great Britain's Sky Brown.

Skateboarding (Street).gamesContext: Skateboarding returns for its third straight Summer Games in 2028 and is now a permanent part of the program, after appearing as a discretionary sport at Tokyo and Paris. The 2028 Games will be something of a homecoming, since the sport has deep roots in Southern California. There are four medal events, men's and women's Street and men's and women's Park, each with 22 athletes, for 88 skaters in total. Qualification runs through the World Skateboarding Rankings and a final Q-Series of events, and the Men's Street Final is listed as a medal session on July 20. The format follows Paris: preliminaries lead to an eight-skater final, scored on each skater's best run plus their two highest single-trick scores.
Skateboarding (Street).parisRecap: Japan's Yuto Horigome kept his men's Street title at Place de la Concorde on July 29, 2024, two days after the final was postponed by rain. He was in fourth place going into his last attempt and won with a nollie 270 bluntslide on his final trick, moving past Americans Jagger Eaton (silver) and Nyjah Huston (bronze) in a final many called one of the best ever. In women's Street, Japan's teenagers Coco Yoshizawa and Liz Akama took gold and silver, and Brazil's Rayssa Leal won bronze. Australia won both Park events: Keegan Palmer defended his men's title ahead of Tom Schaar (USA) and Augusto Akio (BRA), and Arisa Trew won the women's event ahead of Kokona Hiraki (JPN) and Sky Brown (GBR).

Skateboarding (Park).gamesContext: Skateboarding returns for its third Games appearance in 2028, and it is now a permanent part of the program after two appearances as an optional added sport. The Southern California setting is a homecoming for a sport with deep roots in the region. Park is one of two disciplines alongside street, with men's and women's park each awarding one medal (four skateboarding medal events in total), and each park event is expected to field 22 skaters. Competition runs as a preliminary round followed by a final for the top skaters. Qualification is based on the World Skateboarding Ranking, which began with direct ranking points at a June event in Rome, and final park places will be decided through a 2028 Qualification Series.
Skateboarding (Park).parisRecap: In women's park at Paris 2024, 14-year-old Arisa Trew of Australia won gold with a final-run score of 93.18, making her Australia's youngest-ever gold medalist. The podium was extremely close: Japan's Kokona Hiraki took silver with 92.63 and Great Britain's Sky Brown took bronze with 92.31. In men's park, Australia's Keegan Palmer successfully defended his title with a first-run 93.11 that no one could beat. Tom Schaar of the USA took silver and Brazil's Augusto Akio took bronze, in a final where only two of the eight finalists landed their opening runs.

Climbing.gamesContext: Sport climbing comes back in 2028 for its third Games, and it expands to six medal events: men's and women's Speed, Boulder, and Lead. Tokyo 2020 had one combined event per gender. Paris 2024 split Speed off but kept Boulder and Lead as a single combined event. In 2028 each discipline gets its own medals for the first time. The athlete quota also grows, and the qualification system will decide whether athletes can enter more than one event. Boulder and Lead each run as a semifinal followed by a final. Speed starts with a qualification round, then moves to knockout head-to-head races from the quarterfinals through the final.
Climbing.parisRecap: Speed set records in Paris. In women's qualifying, Aleksandra Mirosław of Poland broke her own world record and then broke it again, running 6.06 seconds. She went on to win gold, with Deng Lijuan of China taking silver and her Polish teammate Aleksandra Kałucka bronze. The men's Speed final was the fastest men's race on record: Veddriq Leonardo of Indonesia beat Wu Peng of China 4.75 to 4.77, and American Sam Watson set a world record on his way to bronze. In the combined Boulder and Lead, Janja Garnbret of Slovenia added a second straight title to her Tokyo win, ahead of Brooke Raboutou of the USA and Jessica Pilz of Austria. Toby Roberts of Great Britain won the men's event over Sorato Anraku of Japan and Jakob Schubert of Austria.

Golf.gamesContext: Golf returns for its fourth straight Games since coming back to the program in 2016, and it adds a third medal event in 2028. Men and women each play a 72-hole individual stroke play event over four rounds. The new Mixed Team event, approved by the IOC Executive Board, is played between the men's and women's competitions. It is a 36-hole team event with 18 holes of foursomes (alternate shot) and 18 holes of four-ball, with men and women playing on the same national teams. The headline change from Paris 2024, where only the two individual events were held, is the debut of this mixed-gender team medal.
Golf.parisRecap: At Le Golf National, world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler of the USA came back from off the lead with a final-round 9-under 62. That round matched the course record, included a back nine of 29 and gave him gold at 19 under. Britain's Tommy Fleetwood, the crowd favorite, shot 66 and holed a par putt on the last hole to take silver one shot back. Japan's Hideki Matsuyama won bronze, while Jon Rahm and defending champion Xander Schauffele, who shared the 54-hole lead, missed the podium. In the women's event, New Zealand's Lydia Ko won gold ahead of Germany's Esther Henseleit (silver) and China's Janet Lin (bronze). Ko added the gold to her silver from 2016 and bronze from Tokyo, making her the first golfer to win all three medals and the most decorated golfer in Games history. The win also gave her the final point she needed for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

Rugby Sevens.gamesContext: Rugby sevens returns for its fourth straight Summer Games in 2028, with two medal events: one men's and one women's tournament of 12 teams each. The United States qualifies automatically in both as host. Other places come from the top four eligible teams in the 2027 SVNS World Championship standings, six regional qualifiers, and a final repechage. Each tournament runs pool play, then quarterfinals with classification matches, then semifinals and placing games, and ends with the bronze and gold medal matches. One change from Paris 2024: the women play first this time (July 12-15, 2028), followed by the men (July 16-18). In Paris the men's tournament came first.
Rugby Sevens.parisRecap: In the men's final, host France beat two-time defending champion Fiji 28-7, ending Fiji's unbeaten record at the Games. Antoine Dupont came off the bench to score two tries and set up a third, and the win gave France its first gold of Paris 2024. South Africa took the men's bronze. In the women's final, New Zealand came from behind to beat Canada 19-12 and keep the title it won in Tokyo. The United States won its first-ever medal in the sport, a bronze, by beating Australia 14-12 with a try in the final seconds. Ilona Maher's high profile helped make that team one of the big stories of the Games. Rugby sevens set attendance records in Paris, with more than 500,000 fans at the Stade de France.

Badminton.gamesContext: Badminton returns at the 2028 Summer Games with the same five medal events as Paris 2024: men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles and mixed doubles. The format again starts with a group play stage, followed by knockout rounds (round of 16 in singles, then quarterfinals, semifinals and gold and bronze medal matches). The governing body has approved qualification rules for a quota of 172 players (86 men and 86 women), including two host-country places. Qualifying is based on a dedicated ranking list built from results between 3 May 2027 and 30 April 2028 and published on 2 May 2028. The men's singles title will change hands: Paris and Tokyo champion Viktor Axelsen has retired from competitive badminton because of chronic back problems, so there will be no title defense. Lee Yang, half of the Chinese Taipei men's doubles champions, has also retired.
Badminton.parisRecap: China led the Paris 2024 badminton competition. Zheng Si Wei and Huang Ya Qiong beat Korea's Kim Won Ho and Jeong Na Eun 21-8, 21-11 in the mixed doubles final, and Japan's Yuta Watanabe and Arisa Higashino took bronze. China also filled both finalist spots in women's doubles, where Chen Qingchen and Jia Yifan won gold and Japan took bronze. In women's singles, Korea's An Se-Young beat China's He Bingjiao 21-13, 21-16 for gold, with Indonesia's Gregoria Mariska Tunjung winning bronze. Viktor Axelsen of Denmark defended his men's singles title by beating Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn, and Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia beat India's Lakshya Sen for bronze. Chinese Taipei's Lee Yang and Wang Chi-Lin became the first pair to win men's doubles at two straight Games, beating China's Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang 21-17, 18-21, 21-19, while Malaysia took bronze.

Judo.gamesContext: Judo comes back for the 2028 Summer Games with 15 medal events, the same as Paris 2024: seven men's weight categories (-60kg to +100kg), seven women's weight categories (-48kg to +78kg), and one mixed team event, a format first used in Tokyo. The competition is scheduled for July 15 to 22, 2028. Each individual weight class is decided in a single day, with elimination rounds in the morning, then repechage, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal bouts in the evening. The mixed team event closes the program. As host nation, the USA gets 14 quota places, one in each individual weight category, plus a mixed team spot. France arrives as the only nation ever to win the mixed team title. Teddy Riner has said he is aiming for another title, but his participation is not confirmed.
Judo.parisRecap: Host nation France won the most judo medals in Paris. Teddy Riner took his third individual heavyweight gold, beating Kim Min-Jong of Korea in the final. The next day he won the deciding bout against Tatsuru Saito as France came back to beat Japan in the mixed team final, a repeat of the Tokyo final. That gave Riner a fifth career gold, tying the French record, while Korea and Brazil took the two team bronzes. Japan won three individual golds: Hifumi Abe defended his -66kg title, and Takanori Nagase (-81kg) and Natsumi Tsunoda (-48kg) also won. Several countries won their first judo titles: Canada's Christa Deguchi took the women's -57kg, Slovenia's Andreja Leški the -63kg, Croatia's Barbara Matić the -70kg, Italy's Alice Bellandi the -78kg, Brazil's Beatriz Souza the +78kg, Uzbekistan's Diyora Keldiyorova the -52kg, and Azerbaijan won two golds through Hidayət Heydərov and Zelym Kotsoiev.

Fencing.gamesContext: Fencing has been on the program at every modern Summer Games since 1896 and returns in 2028 with 12 medal events, the same as Paris 2024: individual and team events in épée, foil and sabre for men and women. Competition is scheduled for July 15-23, 2028, though organizers say dates may change. Individual events are direct-elimination brackets from the Table of 64 through the semifinals and medal bouts, with individual bouts going to 15 touches. Team events start at the Table of 8 and end with bronze and gold medal matches plus classification bouts, with team matches going to 45 touches. Home interest will center on the United States women's foil program, which won both individual and team gold in Paris.
Fencing.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, Lee Kiefer of the United States successfully defended her individual foil title by beating teammate Lauren Scruggs in an all-American final, with Canada's Eleanor Harvey taking bronze. The U.S. women then won team foil gold over Italy. Japan had a breakthrough Games: Koki Kano beat France's Yannick Borel for individual épée gold, and Japan won men's team foil gold over Italy. Hungary edged Japan in overtime to win men's team épée. Hong Kong won two individual golds, with Edgar Cheung defending his foil title and Vivian Kong winning women's épée. Korea's Oh Sang-Uk won men's sabre, and Korea also won the men's sabre team event over Hungary. In women's sabre, the host nation went one-two with Manon Apithy-Brunet ahead of Sara Balzer, and Ukraine, led by individual bronze medalist Olha Kharlan, won women's sabre team gold over Korea. Italy won women's team épée over France.

Taekwondo.gamesContext: Taekwondo returns at the 2028 Summer Games with eight medal events, the same weight categories as Paris 2024. Men compete at -58kg, -68kg, -80kg and +80kg, and women at -49kg, -57kg, -67kg and +67kg. Each day features one men's and one women's weight class. Morning sessions cover the Round of 32 and Round of 16. Later sessions cover the quarterfinals, semifinals, repechage contests, both bronze medal contests and the gold medal contest. The repechage gives fighters who lost to the two finalists a route to one of the two bronze medals awarded in each category. South Korea is historically the sport's most successful nation, ahead of China.
Taekwondo.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, France's Althéa Laurin won the women's heavyweight title with a high kick in the final seconds against Uzbekistan's Svetlana Osipova. Laurin had won bronze in Tokyo, and this was France's first-ever gold in taekwondo. Thailand's Panipak Wongpattanakit won the women's flyweight title again, beating China's Guo Qing in the final. South Korea won two golds, with Park Tae-Jun in men's flyweight and Kim Yu-Jin in women's featherweight. Iran also had a strong Games: Arian Salimi won men's heavyweight gold over Great Britain's Caden Cunningham, and Iran took silver through Mehran Barkhordari and Nahid Kiyani. The champions came from many different countries, including Firas Katoussi of Tunisia (men's welterweight), Ulugbek Rashitov of Uzbekistan (men's featherweight) and Viviana Márton of Hungary (women's welterweight).

Wrestling.gamesContext: Wrestling returns at the 2028 Summer Games with 18 medal events, the same lineup as Paris 2024: six men's Greco-Roman classes (60, 67, 77, 87, 97, 130kg), six men's freestyle classes (57, 65, 74, 86, 97, 125kg) and six women's freestyle classes (50, 53, 57, 62, 68, 76kg). Each class runs as a single-elimination bracket over two days. Day one covers the round of 16, quarterfinals and semifinals. Day two has repechage bouts, two bronze-medal matches and the gold-medal final. The schedule opens with Greco-Roman and women's freestyle on July 24, 2028. Greco-Roman wraps up around July 27, while men's and women's freestyle run through July 30. Each country can enter at most one wrestler per weight class, with places earned through United World Wrestling qualifying events. As host, the United States brings a strong freestyle program, led by its Paris 2024 gold medalists in women's freestyle.
Wrestling.parisRecap: Japan dominated Paris 2024 with eight golds across all three styles. In Greco-Roman, Kenichiro Fumita won 60kg and Nao Kusaka won 77kg. In men's freestyle, Rei Higuchi took 57kg over Spencer Lee of the USA and Kotaro Kiyooka took 65kg. In women's freestyle, Akari Fujinami (53kg), Tsugumi Sakurai (57kg), Sakura Motoki (62kg) and Yuka Kagami (76kg) all won gold, with Kagami beating Kennedy Blades of the USA in the 76kg final. Cuba's Mijaín López won the Greco-Roman 130kg title over Yasmani Acosta of Chile, his fifth straight title at the Games and a record for an individual event. Iran's Greco-Roman golds came from Saeid Esmaeili at 67kg and Mohammadhadi Saravi at 97kg. Semen Novikov of Bulgaria won 87kg. In freestyle, Georgia's Geno Petriashvili took 125kg, Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov won 97kg, Bulgaria's Magomed Ramazanov won 86kg and Uzbekistan's Razambek Zhamalov won 74kg. For the USA, Amit Elor won women's 68kg and Sarah Hildebrandt won women's 50kg over Cuba's Yusneylys Guzmán, after the original finalist was disqualified for missing weight.

Handball.gamesContext: Handball returns at the 2028 Summer Games with two medal events, a men's and a women's tournament, and the same 12-team field per gender as Paris 2024: 24 teams and 336 athletes in total, with 14-player squads. Each tournament starts with a preliminary round and moves into knockout play: quarterfinals, semifinals, then bronze and gold medal matches. The host nation gets one automatic quota place per gender, so the United States is set to field both a men's and a women's team, a rare appearance for a country outside the sport's European heartland. The other places are filled through continental qualification events and three qualification tournaments per gender held in spring 2028.
Handball.parisRecap: Denmark dominated the men's tournament and beat Germany 39-26 in the gold medal match, the most lopsided final in memory. Mathias Gidsel starred for the Danes, and the final was the last match of Mikkel Hansen's career and Niklas Landin Jacobsen's last international game. Spain took men's bronze. In the women's final, Norway beat defending Tokyo champion France 29-21 for its first gold since London 2012 and a fifth straight medal in the event, with Henny Reistad scoring eight goals; Denmark won women's bronze, finishing with medals in both tournaments.

Hockey.gamesContext: Hockey returns for the 2028 Summer Games with two medal events, a men's tournament and a women's tournament. Each has 12 teams of 16 players, for 384 athletes in all. Teams qualify through a host-nation place, the FIH Hockey Pro League, continental championships, or two eight-team qualification tournaments in early 2028. The 2028 session schedule adds a play-in round between the pool stage and the quarterfinals, followed by semifinals and bronze and gold medal matches. This is a change from Paris 2024, where the top four teams from each six-team pool went straight to the quarterfinals. The Netherlands will be defending both titles.
Hockey.parisRecap: The Netherlands won both hockey titles at Paris 2024, a gold double. In the men's final the Dutch drew 1-1 with Germany and won the shoot-out 3-1, giving them their first men's gold since 2000 and their third overall. India beat Spain to take men's bronze. In the women's final China led for most of the match before the Netherlands drew level and won the shoot-out, defending their title and extending their record to five women's golds. China took a breakthrough silver, and Argentina won bronze by drawing 2-2 with Belgium and winning the shoot-out 3-1.

Water Polo.gamesContext: Water polo returns at the 2028 Games. It has been on the program since 1900, which makes it the oldest team sport at the Summer Games. There are two medal events, a men's tournament and a women's tournament. Each one starts with preliminary matches and then moves to knockout rounds: quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal matches. The main change from Paris 2024 is that the women's field grows from 10 to 12 teams, so for the first time both tournaments have the same number of teams. The qualification system was confirmed by the IOC and World Aquatics in April 2025.
Water Polo.parisRecap: In the men's tournament, Serbia beat its regional rival Croatia 13-11 in the gold medal match on the last day of competition. This was Serbia's third straight title, even though it lost group games to Australia, Spain and Hungary. Serbia's Dusan Mandic was the top scorer with 26 goals and was named MVP. The United States beat Hungary for bronze, the American men's first medal since 2008. In the women's tournament, Spain won every match and beat Australia 11-9 in the final for its first gold in women's water polo, after taking silver in Tokyo. The Netherlands won bronze, and the United States, champions at the previous three Games, finished off the podium.

Table Tennis.gamesContext: Table tennis returns at the 2028 Games with six medal events, up from five in Paris: men's and women's singles, mixed doubles, men's and women's doubles (back for the first time since 2004, after team events replaced them from Beijing 2008), and a new mixed team event. The mixed team event takes the place of the separate men's and women's team competitions. Its format was first used at the ITTF Mixed Team World Cup in December 2023, and in 2028 it runs from a group stage of four groups into quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal matches. The singles draws start at a round of 64 and are single-elimination through to bronze and gold medal matches, and the doubles events run from a round of 16. The main storyline is whether anyone can break China's hold on the sport.
Table Tennis.parisRecap: China won all five gold medals at Paris 2024. Fan Zhendong took men's singles gold over Sweden's Truls Möregårdh, and France's Félix Lebrun won bronze in front of a home crowd. Möregårdh's run to the final, which included knocking out the top seed, was the biggest upset of the tournament. Chen Meng kept her women's singles title by beating teammate Sun Yingsha in an all-China final, and Japan's Hina Hayata won bronze. China also won both team golds, beating Sweden in the men's final (France took bronze) and Japan in the women's final (Korea took bronze). In mixed doubles, China beat North Korea for gold and South Korea won bronze.

Weightlifting.gamesContext: Weightlifting returns at the 2028 Summer Games with an expanded program of 12 medal events, six for men and six for women, up from 10 events at Paris 2024. The International Weightlifting Federation redrew the bodyweight categories for 2028: men compete at 65kg, 75kg, 85kg, 95kg, 110kg and +110kg, and women at 53kg, 61kg, 69kg, 77kg, 86kg and +86kg. That means none of the Paris divisions carries over unchanged. Each event is a single session in which every lifter gets three snatch attempts and three clean and jerk attempts, and the best combined total wins. A new, tougher qualification system approved in early 2026 caps the field at 120 lifters, 60 men and 60 women, spread across the 12 categories.
Weightlifting.parisRecap: China topped Paris 2024 with five of the 10 golds: Li Fabin (men's featherweight), Liu Huanhua (men's heavyweight), Hou Zhihui (women's flyweight), Luo Shifang (women's lightweight) and Li Wenwen (women's super-heavyweight). Georgia's Lasha Talakhadze won his third straight super-heavyweight title with a 470kg total (215kg snatch, 255kg clean and jerk), ahead of Armenia's Varazdat Lalayan and Bahrain's Gor Minasyan. In the women's middleweight, 21-year-old Olivia Reeves of the USA won gold with a 262kg total and set a Games-record snatch, beating Colombia's Mari Sánchez and Ecuador's Angie Palacios; teammate Hampton Morris took bronze in the men's featherweight. Other champions were Indonesia's Rizki Juniansyah, Bulgaria's Karlos Nasar and Norway's Solfrid Koanda, who won the women's heavyweight ahead of Egypt's Sara Samir.

Archery.gamesContext: Archery returns at the 2028 Summer Games with six medal events, one more than in Paris. Compound archery gets its first-ever medal through a new compound mixed team event, added in April 2025, and it joins the five recurve events: men's and women's individual, men's and women's team, and mixed team. As in past Games, each discipline starts with a ranking (qualification) round that sets the seeding for head-to-head elimination brackets. Those brackets run from the individual 1/32 rounds through the quarterfinals and semifinals to the bronze and gold medal matches. The compound debut is a big storyline for nations whose compound archers usually outperform their recurve archers, such as India, which has never won an archery medal at the Games.
Archery.parisRecap: The Republic of Korea won all five archery golds at Paris 2024, its best archery result ever at a single Games. Im Si-hyeon won three golds (women's individual, women's team and mixed team) and beat teammate Nam Su-hyeon in an all-Korean individual final. Kim Wu-Jin also won three golds, finishing with a shoot-off win over American Brady Ellison in the men's individual final, while Lee U-Seok took bronze. Host nation France made the podium twice, with men's team silver and a women's individual bronze for Lisa Barbelin. China, Germany, Türkiye and Mexico also won medals in the team events, and the United States added a mixed team bronze.

Canoe Slalom.gamesContext: Canoe slalom returns at the 2028 Games with the same six medal events contested in Paris: men's and women's kayak single (K1), canoe single (C1) and kayak cross, with 82 athlete quota places split equally between men and women. K1 and C1 run as heats over two runs, followed by a semifinal and final. Kayak cross, which debuted in Paris, makes its second appearance, with head-to-head knockout racing from a first round and repechage through the quarterfinals to the finals. Slalom is scheduled to start on July 14, the day of the Opening Ceremony, and will be one of the first sports to award medals on July 15. The K1 finals are on July 15-16, the C1 finals on July 18-19, and both kayak cross finals on July 22.
Canoe Slalom.parisRecap: Australia's Jess Fox won both the women's K1 and C1 in Paris 2024, beating Klaudia Zwolinska and Elena Lilik respectively for gold. She became the first woman to win the canoe-kayak double at a single Games and the most successful slalom paddler in the sport's history at the Games. Her sister Noemie Fox won the first-ever women's kayak cross final ahead of France's Angele Hug, while Britain's Kimberley Woods took bronze in both K1 and kayak cross. In the men's events, New Zealand's Finn Butcher won the first men's kayak cross ahead of Joe Clarke, Italy's Giovanni De Gennaro won K1 ahead of home paddler Titouan Castryck, and France's Nicolas Gestin won C1 gold ahead of Adam Burgess and Matej Benus. USA's Evy Leibfarth won bronze in women's C1.

Canoe Sprint.gamesContext: Canoe sprint returns at the 2028 Summer Games with 10 medal events, split evenly between men and women. The International Canoe Federation says the sprint program will not change from Paris 2024: men's and women's K1, K2, K4, C1 and C2 races, with the men's singles over 1000m (K1 and C1), the women's C1 over 200m, and every other event over 500m. Races move from heats and quarterfinals through semifinals to A finals. The ICF currently lists sprint racing for 25 to 29 July 2028, and canoeing as a whole will award 16 medals in sprint, slalom and kayak cross.
Canoe Sprint.parisRecap: New Zealand's Lisa Carrington won the women's K1 500m in a new Games-best time and also won the K2 500m with Alicia Hoskin and the women's K4 500m. Her total of eight career golds tied the all-time canoeing record. The women's K2 500m ended in a photo-finish tie for bronze, so Germany and a second Hungarian crew shared third place. Czechia won both men's singles 1000m races: Josef Dostal had a surprise win in the K1 ahead of Hungary's Adam Varga and Balint Kopasz, and Martin Fuksa took the C1 ahead of Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz. Germany won both men's kayak team boats, China won the men's and women's C2 500m, and Canada's Katie Vincent won the women's C1 200m by a tiny margin over American Nevin Harrison.

Cycling Road (Road Race).gamesContext: Road cycling returns at the 2028 Games with four medal events, the same lineup as Paris 2024: men's and women's road races (mass-start, single-day races) and men's and women's individual time trials. The time trials open the program on July 19, 2028, and the women's and men's road races follow on July 22 and 23. Organizers have confirmed that the road races run from the Pacific coast inland to an uphill finish in the Griffith Park hills, but the full routes had not been published at last check. Media previews have named Slovenia's Tadej Pogacar as a possible men's contender chasing his first gold at the Games. Reigning women's champion Kristen Faulkner could defend her title on home roads, though no 2028 participation is confirmed.
Cycling Road (Road Race).parisRecap: Belgium's Remco Evenepoel won the men's road race a week after taking the time trial, becoming the first man to win both titles at one Games. He attacked on the climb to Montmartre, rode alone over the last 15 km and survived a puncture inside the final 4 km. He still won by more than a minute ahead of French riders Valentin Madouas and Christophe Laporte, on a course of about 273 km, the longest in the event's history at the Games. In the women's race, American Kristen Faulkner, a late replacement on the US team, made a winning attack in the last few kilometers and finished 58 seconds clear. Marianne Vos of the Netherlands took silver and Belgium's Lotte Kopecky took bronze after a photo finish. Faulkner's win was the first US medal of any color in the road race since 1984 in Los Angeles. In the time trials, Australia's Grace Brown won the women's gold and Evenepoel won the men's, ahead of Filippo Ganna and Wout Van Aert.

Cycling Road (Time Trial).gamesContext: Road cycling returns at the 2028 Games with the road race and the individual time trial. The time trial has two medal events, one for men and one for women. It is scheduled for July 19, 2028, a few days before the road races on July 22–23. Each rider sets off alone at intervals against the clock, and the fastest time wins, with no heats or qualifying rounds. The event looks the same as it did at Paris 2024. The defending women's champion, Grace Brown, retired at the end of the 2024 season, so a new women's champion is guaranteed. Remco Evenepoel and Filippo Ganna are possible men's contenders based on past results, but neither is confirmed to compete.
Cycling Road (Time Trial).parisRecap: The Paris 2024 time trials were held on July 27, 2024 through central Paris in steady rain, and several riders crashed on the slippery roads. Remco Evenepoel of Belgium won the men's race ahead of Italy's Filippo Ganna, and his teammate Wout Van Aert took bronze. A week later Evenepoel also won the road race, making him the first man to win both road events at the same Games. Australia's Grace Brown won the women's race in 39:38.24, ahead of Anna Henderson of Great Britain and Chloé Dygert of the USA. Brown and Evenepoel both went on to win the world time trial titles in Zurich that September, becoming the first riders to win the world and Games time trial titles in the same year.

Cycling Track.gamesContext: Track cycling is back for the 2028 Summer Games. Racing is scheduled from about July 25 to July 30, 2028, on a 250-meter banked wooden track. The program is expected to stay at 12 medal events, the same as Paris 2024: six for men and six for women (team sprint, sprint, keirin, team pursuit, omnium and madison). Sprint events run from qualifying through knockout rounds with repechages to semifinals and finals. The keirin goes first round and repechage, quarterfinals, then semifinal and final. Team events start with qualifying, move to a first round and finish with finals, and the omnium is held on a single day. Cycling's overall rider quota stays the same as in 2024. Projected storylines include whether Harrie Lavreysen of the Netherlands and Ellesse Andrews of New Zealand can defend their sprint titles, and whether the home United States team can repeat its Paris golds in the women's endurance events.
Cycling Track.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, Harrie Lavreysen won three golds: the Netherlands team sprint (in a world-record 40.949), the individual sprint and the keirin. Australia's Matthew Richardson took silver behind him in both the sprint and the keirin. Ellesse Andrews of New Zealand won the women's sprint and keirin. Great Britain won the women's team sprint in a world-record 45.186, and Emma Finucane added bronzes in the sprint and keirin. Australia set a world record in the men's team pursuit heats and went on to beat Great Britain for gold. In the women's team pursuit, the United States beat New Zealand, and Jennifer Valente won the women's omnium for the US. In the other endurance events, Portugal won the men's madison, Italy won the women's madison, and France's Benjamin Thomas won the men's omnium ahead of Portugal's Iuri Leitao.

BMX Freestyle.gamesContext: BMX Freestyle returns for its third appearance at the 2028 Summer Games, having first been added to the program at Tokyo 2020. Two medal events are planned, men's park and women's park, with a combined qualification session followed by a combined final session a day later. Riders are judged on difficulty, execution and creativity, and at Paris 2024 each finalist got two 60-second runs with only the better score counting. The 2028 program brings the discipline to Southern California, widely seen as the birthplace of BMX culture. The session schedule shows no format change from Paris.
BMX Freestyle.parisRecap: Both park finals were held on July 31, 2024 at the urban park at La Concorde in Paris. In the men's final, José Torres Gil of Argentina took gold with a clean first run of 94.82. Reigning world champion Kieran Reilly of Great Britain was close behind for silver at 93.91, and home favorite Anthony Jeanjean of France won bronze with 93.76, making it one of the tightest podiums of the Games. In the women's event, 19-year-old Deng Yawen won China's first title in the discipline with 92.60, posting the top score of the final on both of her runs. Perris Benegas of the USA took silver with 90.70 and Natalya Diehm of Australia took bronze with 88.80. Pre-event favorite Hannah Roberts of the USA crashed and missed the medals, and Tokyo 2020 champion Charlotte Worthington of Great Britain did not make it out of qualification.

BMX Racing.gamesContext: BMX racing returns for its sixth straight Summer Games. It has been on the program since 2008, and Southern California is widely seen as the birthplace of BMX culture. There are two medal events, men's and women's BMX racing, the same as Paris 2024. The published session schedule runs the competition over two sessions: quarterfinals and last chance runs first, then semifinals and finals, where riders race short, fast heats over a dirt track full of jumps and banked turns. France arrives as the defending power after sweeping the men's podium in Paris, but no 2028 rosters have been confirmed.
BMX Racing.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, France swept the men's podium in front of a home crowd at Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines. Joris Daudet won gold, Sylvain André took silver and Romain Mahieu took bronze. The three Frenchmen were also the top three qualifiers, and the sweep finally brought France medals in an event that had long escaped them. Daudet, competing at his fourth Games, said he planned to retire afterward. Australia's Saya Sakakibara won the women's title in a comeback ride that was widely celebrated, ahead of Manon Veenstra of the Netherlands in silver and Zoé Claessens of Switzerland in bronze. In a storyline that drew a lot of attention, Sakakibara and Mahieu, who are a couple, both won medals on the same night.

Equestrian.gamesContext: Equestrian returns at the 2028 Games with three disciplines, dressage, eventing and jumping, each awarding a team and an individual medal, for six medal events. It is one of the few sports where men and women compete in the same events for the same medals, and quota places are not split by gender. Dressage runs from Grand Prix qualifier days to a Grand Prix Special team final and a Grand Prix Freestyle individual final. Jumping holds separate team and individual qualifiers and finals. Eventing runs dressage over two days, then cross-country, then jumping finals for the team and individual medals. The eventing format came under review for 2028: the governing body sent a new hybrid format to the organizers after being told to cut cost and complexity. Qualification runs through the 2026 world championships, 2027 continental championships, the 2027 Pan American Games and designated qualifying events.
Equestrian.parisRecap: Germany led equestrian at Paris 2024 with four golds and a silver, including the individual gold in all three disciplines. Michael Jung became the first rider to win three individual eventing titles, ahead of Christopher Burton and Laura Collett. Collett and Jung both set record eventing dressage scores, and Great Britain won team eventing gold ahead of France and Japan. In dressage, Germany won team gold over Denmark and Great Britain, and Jessica von Bredow-Werndl took individual gold ahead of teammate Isabell Werth and Britain's Lottie Fry. In jumping, Great Britain won team gold ahead of the United States and France. The individual jumping final went to a three-way jump-off: Christian Kukuk won his first major medal by going clear, just 0.04 seconds faster than Steve Guerdat, with Maikel van der Vleuten taking bronze.

Rowing.gamesContext: Rowing returns at the 2028 Games with 12 classic events, six for men and six for women: single sculls, double sculls, pair, four, quadruple sculls and eight. The regatta is scheduled for July 15-22. Races will be 1,500 metres instead of the usual 2,000 metres, the shortest course in the sport's history at the Games. Crews race heats, then repechages, quarterfinals and semifinals where the event uses them, before ranking finals (A through F in the singles) that decide the medals and final placings. The men's and women's lightweight double sculls from Paris 2024 have been dropped. Beach sprint coastal rowing (men's solo, women's solo and mixed double sculls) is being added as a separate discipline, scheduled for July 24-25. Most boats will qualify at the 2027 World Rowing Championships in Lucerne, followed by continental and final qualification regattas.
Rowing.parisRecap: The Netherlands led the Paris 2024 regatta with four golds: men's quadruple sculls, women's pair, women's four, and Karolien Florijn in the women's single, where she beat Emma Twigg (NZL) and Viktorija Senkuté (LTU). The Dutch also took silver in the men's double, men's eight and women's quad. Great Britain won three golds (men's eight, women's quadruple sculls and women's lightweight double), and Romania won two (men's double and women's eight) as well as silver in the women's double, pair and lightweight double. Oliver Zeidler (GER) won the men's single ahead of Yauheni Zalaty (AIN) and Simon van Dorp (NED). The other golds went to the United States in the men's four, Croatia in the men's pair, New Zealand in the women's double and Ireland in the men's lightweight double, the last time that event was held.

Rowing Coastal.gamesContext: Coastal rowing makes its debut at the 2028 Games in the beach sprint format. It is the first time rowing will run two separate disciplines at one Games, and the first time a Games rowing event will be raced on the open ocean. There are three medal events: men's solo, women's solo and mixed double sculls. The mixed double is the first mixed-gender rowing event ever held at the Games. Each race starts with a sprint across the sand to the boat, then a row of about 250m out through the surf to a turn buoy and back, then a final run up the beach to the finish line. Crews race two time trials to set seeding for head-to-head knockout rounds (last 16, then a final eight). Places are earned mainly at the 2027 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Oeiras, Portugal, and at continental qualifiers. Contenders to watch based on recent world finals (not confirmed for 2028): American Christopher Bak, the most decorated beach sprinter so far, who won the men's solo world title in 2024 and 2025. At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, China won the men's solo through Liu Jiayu, Australia's Isabella Scammell won the women's solo, and Germany beat two-time champions Lithuania in the mixed double sculls.
Rowing Coastal.parisRecap: Coastal rowing was not on the Paris 2024 program, so there are no Paris medal results for this sport. The 2028 Games will be its first appearance. Rowing at Paris 2024 was limited to the classic 2,000m flatwater events. Beach sprint's top level before 2028 has been the annual World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals. In 2024, Christopher Bak (USA) won the men's solo and Magdalena Lobnig (Austria) won the women's solo there.

Shooting (R/P).gamesContext: Rifle and pistol shooting is back for the 2028 Games. Shooting as a whole has 15 medal events, and 10 of them are rifle/pistol: men's and women's 10m air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions and 10m air pistol, the men's 25m rapid fire pistol, the women's 25m pistol, and mixed team 10m air rifle and 10m air pistol. Every event runs a qualification round followed by a final. Qualification works the same way as at Paris 2024, and the athlete quota stays at 340 across all shooting. The biggest changes from Paris: the 50m rifle 3 positions finals are standing-only, the 25m rapid fire pistol final grows from six to eight shooters, and the mixed team events drop their separate gold and bronze medal matches. Instead, the top four qualifying teams shoot one combined medal final using elimination. ISSF has also announced "live aiming" displays for rifle and pistol, and athletes start qualifying at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha.
Shooting (R/P).parisRecap: China and South Korea dominated rifle and pistol at Paris 2024. China won the men's air rifle (Sheng Lihao), men's air pistol (Xie Yu), men's 50m rifle 3 positions (Liu Yukun), men's rapid fire pistol (Li Yuehong, with Wang Xinjie taking bronze) and the mixed team air rifle. Sheng took two golds by also winning the mixed team event, beating Korea in the gold medal match. South Korea won all three individual women's pistol and air rifle titles. Ban Hyo-Jin won the women's air rifle over China's Huang Yuting, Oh Ye-Jin and Kim Ye-Ji went one-two in women's air pistol, and Yang Ji-In beat home favourite Camille Jedrzejewski of France in the 25m pistol. India's Manu Bhaker won two bronzes, one in women's air pistol and one in the mixed team air pistol, where Serbia took gold ahead of Türkiye. Switzerland's Chiara Leone won the women's 50m rifle 3 positions ahead of Sagen Maddalena of the USA.

Shooting (Shotgun).gamesContext: Shotgun shooting returns at the 2028 Summer Games as part of a 15-event shooting program with 340 athlete quota places in total. The shotgun side has five medal events: men's and women's trap, men's and women's skeet, and a mixed team event. The biggest program change from Paris 2024 is that mixed team trap replaces mixed team skeet. It also uses a new final format: the top four teams from qualification all shoot together in a single medal final, instead of separate gold and bronze medal matches. Individual trap and skeet run over two days, with day 1 qualification, then the rest of qualification and the finals on day 2. Qualification for the 2028 Games starts with quota places awarded at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha. The host nation, the United States, comes in with medal momentum after its skeet results in Paris.
Shooting (Shotgun).parisRecap: At Paris 2024, the United States went one-two in men's skeet: Vincent Hancock won gold ahead of teammate Conner Prince, and Chinese Taipei's Lee Meng-Yuan took bronze. Hancock's gold extended his record in the event. In men's trap, Great Britain's Nathan Hales won gold ahead of China's Qi Ying, with bronze for Guatemala's Jean-Pierre Brol. Guatemala had a historic week: Adriana Ruano won women's trap, the country's first gold medal, ahead of Italy's Silvana Stanco and Australia's Penny Smith. Chile's Francisca Crovetto won women's skeet over Great Britain's Amber Rutter, with bronze for Austen Smith of the United States. Italy won the one-time mixed skeet team event ahead of the United States and China, and that event is replaced by mixed team trap for 2028.

Sailing (D/S/M).gamesContext: Sailing comes back at the 2028 Games with the same 10 medal events as Paris 2024. They are split into two blocks. The windsurfing (iQFOiL) and kiteboarding (Formula Kite) events go first, July 16-20. The dinghy, skiff and multihull events follow, July 23-28. This D/S/M group has six medal events: men's one-person dinghy (ILCA 7), women's one-person dinghy (ILCA 6), mixed two-person dinghy (470), men's skiff (49er), women's skiff (49erFX) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17). Each event runs as a multi-day series of fleet races, followed by a finals day where the medals are decided.
Sailing (D/S/M).parisRecap: Paris 2024 sailing was raced off Marseille. Australia's Matt Wearn won the men's one-person dinghy ahead of Cyprus's Pavlos Kontides, with Peru's Stefano Peschiera taking bronze. Marit Bouwmeester of the Netherlands won the women's one-person dinghy, with Denmark's Anne-Marie Rindom second and Norway's Line Høst third. Italy won the mixed multihull ahead of Argentina and New Zealand. Austria won the mixed two-person dinghy, with Japan second and Sweden third. In the men's skiff, Spain took gold, New Zealand silver and the United States bronze.

Sailing (W/K).gamesContext: Kiteboarding (Formula Kite) and windsurfing (iQFOiL) return for their second Games after debuting at Paris 2024. Together they make up four of the 10 sailing medal events: men's and women's kite, and men's and women's windsurfing. The board events open the sailing program as a separate first phase before the boat classes start. Each discipline runs a multi-day qualification series followed by a finals day. Kite medals are scheduled to be decided first, on July 19, 2028, and windsurfing follows on July 20. The main equipment change since Paris is in the iQFOiL class, which has resized its sails for the 2028 cycle: men will race 8 square meter sails, and women will race a newly designed 7.3 square meter sail. The class says the goal is to better match target athlete weights and make the field fairer across body types.
Sailing (W/K).parisRecap: Paris 2024 was the first Games for foiling windsurfing and kiteboarding, with racing on the Marseille waters. In windsurfing, Israel's Tom Reuveny won men's gold ahead of Australia's Grae Morris and Luuc van Opzeeland of the Netherlands. Italy's Marta Maggetti took the women's title, with Israel's Sharon Kantor second and Britain's Emma Wilson third. In the inaugural kite events, Austria's Valentin Bontus won men's gold over Slovenia's Toni Vodišek, with Singapore's Max Maeder taking bronze.
