Britain's Ellie Aldridge won the women's event ahead of home favorite Lauriane Nolot of France and Annelous Lammerts of the Netherlands.

Trampoline Gymnastics.gamesContext: Trampoline gymnastics returns at the 2028 Games. It has been on the Summer Games program since Sydney 2000. There are again two medal events, a men's individual and a women's individual competition, and no change in format from Paris 2024 has been announced. Each event has a qualification round followed by a final, and judges score routines on difficulty, execution and time in the air. The published schedule places the trampoline sessions around Friday, July 21, 2028, with the women's final listed in an evening session.
Trampoline Gymnastics.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, Belarus's Ivan Litvinovich, competing as an Individual Neutral Athlete, won the men's title. He was the first neutral athlete to win gold at those Games and successfully defended the title he won in Tokyo. China's Wang Zisai took silver and Yan Langyu took bronze. In the women's event, Great Britain's Bryony Page won gold, adding to her silver from Rio 2016 and bronze from Tokyo 2020. That made her the only female trampolinist with a full set of medals. Viyaleta Bardzilouskaya (AIN) won silver and Canada's Sophiane Méthot won bronze.

Rhythmic Gymnastics.gamesContext: Rhythmic gymnastics returns in 2028 to Los Angeles, the city where it first became a medal sport in 1984. The group event was added in 1996. The program again has two women's medal events, the individual all-around and the group all-around, with no change from Paris 2024. Each event has a qualification round followed by a final: individual gymnasts perform four apparatus routines in qualification and the top 10 move on to the all-around final. Up to 24 individual gymnasts will compete, with a maximum of two per nation. Places are earned through the 2026 and 2027 World Championships, the 2026-2027 World Cup Series and the 2028 Continental Championships, with host-nation and universality places also available. The sessions take place in the closing days of the 2028 Games.
Rhythmic Gymnastics.parisRecap: Russia and Belarus, which had long dominated the sport, did not compete in Paris, and that opened the door to new champions. Germany's Darja Varfolomeev, the reigning world champion, won the individual all-around with 142.850 points, posting the top score on three of her four apparatus. It was Germany's first gold in the sport. Bulgaria's Boryana Kaleyn took silver and Italy's Sofia Raffaeli won bronze. In the group all-around, China scored 69.800 to win its first-ever gold in rhythmic gymnastics, finishing 0.95 ahead of Israel in second, with Italy third. China became the first non-European nation to win a gold medal in the sport.

Artistic Swimming.gamesContext: Artistic swimming comes back for the 2028 Summer Games with two medal events: a women's duet and a team event that is open to men. Under rule changes adopted for 2022 to 2025, the team has eight members and can include up to two men. The duet medal is decided by combining scores from a technical routine and a free routine. The team medal combines technical, free and acrobatic routines. The competition is expected to run from about July 25 to 29, 2028. One storyline is that more men are competing in the sport, and World Aquatics is now promoting mixed duets and male athletes as teams build toward 2028. Another is whether China can defend both titles it won in Paris.
Artistic Swimming.parisRecap: China won both events at Paris 2024. In the duet, twins Wang Liuyi and Wang Qianyi took gold ahead of Kate Shortman and Isabelle Thorpe of Great Britain, with Bregje and Noortje de Brouwer of the Netherlands taking bronze. China led the team event after the technical and free routines and then sealed its first-ever team gold with the acrobatic routine. The United States took team silver and Spain took bronze. Russia, which had won every gold in the sport since 2000, did not compete, so new champions were guaranteed. Paris 2024 was also the first Games where men were allowed to compete in the team event.

Triathlon.gamesContext: Triathlon returns at the 2028 Games with the same three medal events as Paris 2024: men's individual, women's individual and mixed relay. There are no heats; each event is a single final race. The individual races use the standard distance of a 1.5km swim, 40km bike and 10km run, and 110 athlete quota places are available across both genders. Organizers have unveiled loop-style courses with a surf start and an eight-lap bike leg, and the women's individual race is scheduled to award the very first medals of the 2028 Games.
Triathlon.parisRecap: In the men's race, Great Britain's Alex Yee made a dramatic late comeback. He passed long-time leader and rival Hayden Wilde of New Zealand in the final minute and won by about six seconds, with France's Léo Bergère taking bronze. France's Cassandre Beaugrand won women's gold on home soil, ahead of Switzerland's Julie Derron and Great Britain's Beth Potter. The mixed relay came down to a three-way sprint finish, with Germany edging the United States and Great Britain to win its first gold in the event. The swim legs were held in the Seine around Pont Alexandre III.

Modern Pentathlon.gamesContext: Modern pentathlon returns at the 2028 Games after being approved for the Los Angeles program by the IOC Session in Mumbai, but in a changed format: a head-to-head, ninja-style sprint obstacle race replaces horse riding, alongside fencing, swimming and the laser run (running combined with shooting). There are expected to be two medal events, men's individual and women's individual, each decided through semifinals and then a final. The sport moves back to the start of the Games schedule for the first time since 1992, with four days of competition from July 15 to 18, 2028; the women's final is on day three and the men's final on day four.
Modern Pentathlon.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, competition was held at the Château de Versailles. It was the last edition to include riding, and the first to use the shorter semifinal-and-final format. Egypt's Ahmed El-Gendy set a record score of 1,516 points in his semifinal, then won gold with a world-record total of 1,555 points. That made him the first athlete from Africa to win a medal in the sport. Taishu Sato of Japan took silver and Giorgio Malan of Italy took bronze. On the women's side, Hungary's Michelle Gulyás won gold with a world-record 1,461 points, ahead of France's Élodie Clouvel, who took silver in front of a home crowd, and Seong Seung-Min of Korea, who took bronze.

Mountain Bike.gamesContext: Mountain bike returns to the 2028 Summer Games with the same two medal events contested in Paris 2024: men's cross-country and women's cross-country, each a single mass-start race in which riders complete multiple laps of a rugged, technical course packed with climbs, descents and obstacles. There are no heats or qualifying rounds at the Games, so each race is a one-day final decided in roughly an hour and a half of racing. The published schedule puts the men's race on July 17, 2028 and the women's race on July 18, 2028, both starting at 11:00 PT. The discipline has been on the program since Atlanta 1996, so 2028 marks its second appearance at a U.S.-hosted Summer Games.
Mountain Bike.parisRecap: In Paris 2024, Tom Pidcock (GBR) defended the cross-country title he won in Tokyo. He took the lead early, then punctured and needed a new front wheel, which left him about 40 seconds back. He fought his way back and beat Victor Koretzky (FRA) in a tense final-lap duel, winning in 1:26:22. Koretzky finished 9 seconds behind for silver and Alan Hatherly (RSA) was 11 seconds back for bronze, and Pidcock's aggressive late pass drew boos from the home crowd. A day earlier, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (FRA) dominated the women's race over seven laps to finally win the one major title missing from her career, after disappointments at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020. Haley Batten (USA) took silver, 2:57 behind, and Jenny Rissveds (SWE) won bronze, 3:02 back.

Open Water Swimming.gamesContext: Open water swimming returns at the 2028 Games for its sixth straight edition since its 2008 debut. It keeps the Paris format of two medal events, a men's 10km and a women's 10km, each a single mass-start race in the Pacific Ocean, and it is scheduled early in the Games on July 17-18 (Days 3-4). Each race has 22 quota places, the same as Paris, including one host place, with a maximum of two swimmers per nation. The top three in each 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest qualify automatically, the rest qualify at a spring 2028 qualification event, and swimmers already qualified for the 800m or 1500m freestyle in the pool can also enter. Germany's Florian Wellbrock and Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri finished first and second in the men's 10km at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore, so they are projected contenders, though neither is confirmed for 2028.
Open Water Swimming.parisRecap: At Paris 2024, both 10km races were swum in the River Seine, starting and finishing near Pont Alexandre III, while water quality was under close scrutiny. On August 8, Sharon van Rouwendaal of the Netherlands won the women's race by about five seconds over Australia's Moesha Johnson, with Italy's Ginevra Taddeucci taking bronze. Van Rouwendaal had also won in 2016, making her the first swimmer to win this event twice. On August 9, Hungary's Kristof Rasovszky turned his Tokyo 2020 silver into gold, Hungary's first win in the men's 10km, ahead of Germany's Oliver Klemet, while his teammate David Betlehem took bronze to give Hungary two places on the podium.
